rgb: The scene is a corner kitchen featuring wrap-around upper wooden cabinets above a countertop (~3 to 5 m ahead) with a white microwave in the corner and a white range hood on the right, bounded on the far right by a vertical partition wall opening into an adjacent room with a window and string lights (~0.8 to 1.4 m away). A man in a dark maroon hoodie stands in front of the right counter and range hood, roughly 3 to 5 m from the counter—placing the range hood and counter items out of his arm's reach—and between 3 and 5 m in front of the camera wearer. Across the five frames, the camera wearer turns and shifts rightward while increasing the distance slightly, moving the left-side cabinets out of view and bringing the right partition wall and the man from the far lower-right edge in frame 1 to the center background (out of the camera wearer's arm's reach at ~4 m) by frames 4 and 5. In frames 1 and 2, the man faces toward the camera wearer and away from the range hood, then turns his head counterclockwise over his left shoulder through frames 3 and 4 until he faces and looks directly away from the camera wearer in frame 5. Throughout the sequence, the man's torso crops out below the shoulders at the bottom edge of the frame and occludes the stove area and counter space directly in front of him, while in frame 1 his body is also largely cut off by the right frame boundary.
depth: The monocular depth map captures the 3D geometry of the corner kitchen, separating the far background—the person in the maroon hoodie (bright white/light grey at roughly 3 to 5 m, out of the camera wearer's arm's reach from frame 2 onward) and the vertical partition wall entering on the right in frames 3 to 5 (3 to 5 m away, also out of arm's reach)—from the near upper cabinets, range hood, and countertop microwave (medium grey at roughly 3 to 5 m, out of the other person's arm's reach) and the dark foreground ceiling and adjacent room beyond the partition (under 1.5 m away). Across the five frames, the decreasing brightness and scale of the person and the right wall edge show the camera wearer panning right and moving away from about 3 m to 5 m while the person shifts from the lower-right edge toward the center-left and turns their head from facing the camera wearer (frames 1–3) to profile (frame 4) to facing away from the camera wearer (frame 5). The depth map clearly reveals the continuous planar recession of the intersecting cabinet walls, the protruding box volume of the corner microwave, and the sharp depth discontinuity between the background partition wall and the nearer room to its right, which are harder to judge quantitatively from RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable in assigning noticeably lighter (nearer) values to the person's head than to their hoodie shoulders, bleeding depth halos around the motion-blurred head in frame 3, and flattening small countertop objects like the dish rack and bottles into the foreground.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete background and countertop objects against an unlabelled black background, detecting the person in the lower background (roughly 3 to 5 m from the camera wearer, cropped at the chest/shoulders by the bottom frame border) alongside kitchen items situated about 3 to 5 m behind the person. In frame 1, the person at the bottom-right partially occludes a purple mask over the white range hood above them (~4 m away); in frame 2, as the person shifts left into full view (~4 m away, facing toward the camera wearer), the map delineates a cyan bottle (~4 m away, just to the left of the person's shoulder and out of their arm's reach), a purple microwave (~4 m away in the corner), and a bowl on top of the microwave; in frame 4, it detects a green 'sink' mask at the bottom-left (~4 m away) as the person turns their head left; and in frame 5, only the distant person (~5 m away, looking away from the camera wearer) is segmented. These pixel-level masks make it easy to separate overlapping silhouettes—such as the narrow bottle between the person's left shoulder and the microwave in frame 2—that blend into the cluttered countertop in RGB. However, the map is unreliable across frames: it completely misses all objects during the motion blur of frame 3, misclassifies the overhead range hood as a 'microwave' in frame 1 and a 'tv' in frame 2, mislabels the corner microwave area as a 'sink' in frame 4, and omits the cabinets, partition wall, and countertop clutter.
pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, rendering only sparse, fragmented yellow body keypoints in frames 2 and 4 and no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. Because the person stands very far from the camera wearer (roughly 3 to 5 m away) and is occluded below the upper chest by the bottom border of the egocentric view, their arms and hands remain completely out of view below the frame even though the kitchen counter and bottle (~3 to 5 m in front of them) are out of their arm's reach. In frame 2, a partial yellow shoulder-and-neck structure appears near the bottom-right where the person faces toward the camera wearer and away from the range hood, and in frame 4, a small cluster of tangled yellow torso/head segments appears near the bottom-center as the person turns their head to the left, while frames 1, 3, and 5 contain zero detections despite the person looking directly away from the camera wearer from ~5 m away in frame 5. While the sparse detections in frames 2 and 4 roughly confirm the person's horizontal shift from right to center-left in the lower background, the pose map adds no spatial detail beyond the RGB image and is highly unreliable under severe lower-body truncation, camera-facing orientations, and motion blur.
